parameters.sqlQuery:
-- Frontline roster from the one CS table this credential is known to reach.
-- csn_hr is not accessible, so every Org Browser column that only exists there
-- has been REMOVED rather than left blank. Dropped: HRIS ID, Phone Extension,
-- Seniority Date, Forecast End Date, Birthday, Home Department, Employee Type,
-- Headcount Classification, Employee Profile, Job Title, Manager's HRIS ID,
-- Manager's Work Group, 2nd Level Manager's HRIS ID, Reporting VP,
-- Reporting Senior VP, Shirt Size, Term Date, Work Group 1-10 and 20.
--
-- The duplicated Preferred First/Last Name columns from the export are also
-- dropped - they were a quirk of the Org Browser CSV, identical in every row.
--
-- Source is employee/day grain with the manager chain denormalized per row,
-- so one row per employee needs no join. Verified columns used here:
--   emid employee emailaddress username site hiredate hierarchylevel
--   wgid workgroup parentwgid parentworkgroup mgremid manager mgr2emid
--   manager2 team stillatwayfair lastrundate date datetype
-- 'Day' is the verified datetype literal (internal tickets SDS-767, SDS-938).

WITH latest_snapshot AS (
  SELECT MAX(date) AS snapshot_date
  FROM `wf-gcp-us-ae-cs-prod.cs_reporting.tbl_customer_service_employee_performance_manager`
  WHERE datetype = 'Day'
    AND date BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE('America/Phoenix'), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
                 AND CURRENT_DATE('America/Phoenix')
)
SELECT
  CAST(t.emid AS STRING)                                          AS `Employee ID`,
  -- `employee` is stored "Last, First" (verified in SDS-938)
  TRIM(COALESCE(REGEXP_EXTRACT(TRIM(CAST(t.employee AS STRING)), r',\s*(.+)$'), '')) AS `Preferred First Name`,
  TRIM(COALESCE(REGEXP_EXTRACT(TRIM(CAST(t.employee AS STRING)), r'^([^,]+)'), ''))   AS `Preferred Last Name`,
  LOWER(TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(t.emailaddress AS STRING), '')))       AS `Email Address`,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(t.username AS STRING), ''))                  AS `Sam Account Name`,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(t.site AS STRING), ''))                      AS `Office Location`,
  IFNULL(FORMAT_DATE('%m/%d/%Y', SAFE_CAST(t.hiredate AS DATE)), '') AS `Start Date`,
  CAST(t.hierarchylevel AS STRING)                                AS `Level`,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(t.team AS STRING), ''))                      AS `Team`,
  CAST(t.wgid AS STRING)                                          AS `Work Group ID`,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(t.workgroup AS STRING), ''))                 AS `Work Group`,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(t.parentworkgroup AS STRING), ''))           AS `Parent Work Group`,
  CAST(t.mgremid AS STRING)                                       AS `Manager's Employee ID`,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(t.manager AS STRING), ''))                   AS `Manager's Name`,
  CAST(t.mgr2emid AS STRING)                                      AS `2nd Level Manager's Employee ID`,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(t.manager2 AS STRING), ''))                  AS `2nd Level Manager's Name`,
  CAST(s.snapshot_date AS STRING)                                 AS `Snapshot Date`
FROM `wf-gcp-us-ae-cs-prod.cs_reporting.tbl_customer_service_employee_performance_manager` AS t
CROSS JOIN latest_snapshot AS s
WHERE t.datetype = 'Day'
  AND t.date = s.snapshot_date
  AND t.stillatwayfair IS TRUE
  AND t.emid IS NOT NULL
  -- >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> FRONTLINE SCOPE <<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<
  -- 'Frontline' is the only team literal I could verify (internal ticket
  -- SDS-767 uses AND team = 'Frontline'). Your own org, Multiple Contacts,
  -- may carry a DIFFERENT team value - other internal SQL treats multi-contact
  -- as its own team - so this filter may be too narrow.
  --
  -- The Team column is in the output above precisely so you can see the real
  -- values. If rows are missing, widen this list, e.g.
  --   AND t.team IN ('Frontline', 'Multiple Contacts')
  -- If the run returns ZERO rows, the diagnostic on the failure branch prints
  -- every datetype and team literal in the table - copy the ones you want here.
  AND t.team IN ('Frontline')
  -- >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> END SCOPE <<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.emid ORDER BY t.lastrundate DESC) = 1
ORDER BY `Manager's Name`, `Preferred Last Name`, `Preferred First Name`

-- Runs ONLY when the roster query returns zero rows.
-- Prints the real datetype and team literals plus data freshness, so the scope
-- filter can be corrected from the error message without guesswork.
SELECT
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(datetype AS STRING), '(null)')) AS datetype_value,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(team AS STRING), '(null)'))     AS team_value,
  COUNT(*)                                           AS row_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT emid)                               AS distinct_employees,
  CAST(MAX(date) AS STRING)                          AS max_date,
  DATE_DIFF(CURRENT_DATE('America/Phoenix'), MAX(date), DAY) AS days_stale,
  COUNTIF(COALESCE(stillatwayfair, FALSE))           AS active_rows
FROM `wf-gcp-us-ae-cs-prod.cs_reporting.tbl_customer_service_employee_performance_manager`
WHERE date >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE('America/Phoenix'), INTERVAL 400 DAY)
GROUP BY datetype_value, team_value
ORDER BY row_count DESC
LIMIT 50

parameters.content:
## Frontline Roster - Weekly Monday 4AM Arizona

### Columns were CUT, not left blank
csn_hr is not accessible with this credential, so every Org Browser column that only lives there has been removed. The workflow now writes its own header row containing only what it can actually fill.

REMOVED (18): HRIS ID, Phone Extension, Seniority Date, Forecast End Date, Birthday, Home Department, Employee Type, Headcount Classification, Employee Profile, Job Title, Manager's HRIS ID, Manager's Work Group, 2nd Level Manager's HRIS ID, Reporting VP, Reporting Senior VP, Shirt Size, Term Date, Work Group 1-10 and Work Group 20.

Also removed: the duplicated Preferred First Name / Preferred Last Name columns. They were an Org Browser CSV quirk and identical in every row of your exports.

KEPT (17): Employee ID, Preferred First Name, Preferred Last Name, Email Address, Sam Account Name, Office Location, Start Date, Level, Team, Work Group ID, Work Group, Parent Work Group, Manager's Employee ID, Manager's Name, 2nd Level Manager's Employee ID, 2nd Level Manager's Name, Snapshot Date.

This workflow REPLACES row 1. Your pasted 45-column header row will be overwritten with these 17.

### Source
`wf-gcp-us-ae-cs-prod.cs_reporting.tbl_customer_service_employee_performance_manager` - employee/day grain with the manager chain denormalized per row, so no join is needed. This is the table your original workflow already had working credentials for.

### Scope - read this
The filter is `team IN ('Frontline')`. 'Frontline' is the ONLY team literal I could verify (internal ticket SDS-767). Your own org, Multiple Contacts, may carry a different value, so this may be too narrow.

Team is included as an output column so you can see the real values. If rows look missing, widen the list in the marked FRONTLINE SCOPE block.

If the run returns zero rows, the failure branch queries the table and prints every datetype and team literal it contains, then tells you exactly which line to edit. Read the error text on the failed execution - it hands you the answer.

### Safety
Zero rows means the sheet is NOT cleared and the run fails with that diagnosis. A bad filter can never blank the sheet.

The query takes the newest daily snapshot within 30 days rather than hard-coding yesterday, so a missing weekend snapshot does not produce an empty run. The window is deliberately narrow - widening it would publish stale data as current.

### Schedule
Workflow timezone `America/Phoenix`, cron `0 4 * * 1`. Arizona skips DST so this is 11:00 UTC year-round. Confirm the timezone in Workflow Settings after import.

### After import
Select your BigQuery and Google Sheets credentials on the four credentialed nodes, run manually once, check the summary node for employee_row_count and teams_present, then activate.
